summary: If a yavam does a get, a maamar, yibum or chalitzah, can another such act still count afterward? Rabban Gamliel says no. The Sages say a get or maamar can come after another, but nothing counts after yibum or chalitzah.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel says:

chunks.en: there is no get after a get,
chunks.st: A bill of divorce [get] is not effective when given after a bill of divorce was previously given to a yevama.
chunks.stMore: Once a yevama receives a bill of divorce from a yavam, no bill of divorce given by that yavam to her rival wife or a bill of divorce given to her by a different yavam is of any effect.

chunks.en: and no maamar after a maamar,
chunks.st: And levirate betrothal is not effective after a previous levirate betrothal was performed,

chunks.en: and no marrying after marrying,
chunks.explain: Marrying here means finishing the yibum.
chunks.st: and intercourse with a second yevama is not effective after intercourse with the first one,

chunks.en: and no chalitzah after chalitzah.
chunks.st: and ḥalitza is not effective after ḥalitza was previously performed.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: But the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: there is a get after a get,
chunks.st: A bill of divorce is effective when given after a bill of divorce,

chunks.en: and there is a maamar after a maamar,
chunks.st: and levirate betrothal is effective after levirate betrothal,

chunks.en: but after marrying
chunks.st: but nothing is effective after intercourse

chunks.en: or after chalitzah, nothing counts.
chunks.st: or after ḥalitza.
chunks.stMore: If a yavam has relations with the yevama or performs ḥalitza with her, no other action performed afterward is effective, whether performed by that yavam toward a different yevama or by any yavam with the original yevama.

summary: Examples: a yavam made a maamar and then gave a get, or made a maamar and then did chalitzah. Each time she still needs the other one. A maamar and then marrying is the proper way to do yibum.

chunks.en: How so? If he made a maamar with his yevamah
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: How do these laws work in practice? If a yavam performed levirate betrothal with his yevama,

chunks.en: and gave her a get,
chunks.st: and he later gave her a bill of divorce,

chunks.en: she still needs chalitzah from him.
chunks.st: she nevertheless requires ḥalitza from him. The bill of divorce does not fully exempt her from levirate marriage, as the levirate bond remains intact. If

chunks.en: If he made a maamar and did chalitzah,
chunks.st: he performed levirate betrothal and then ḥalitza,

chunks.en: she needs a get from him.
chunks.st: she requires a bill of divorce from him in order to cancel the levirate betrothal. If the yavam

chunks.en: If he made a maamar and then married her,
chunks.st: performed levirate betrothal and then engaged in intercourse with the yevama,

chunks.en: that is the proper way of the mitzvah.
chunks.st: this is the way to perform levirate marriage in accordance with its mitzva, as the Sages instituted this as the proper procedure for a yavam to perform levirate marriage.

summary: More examples of doing these acts in different orders. After chalitzah, nothing else counts. These rules are the same with one yevamah or two.

chunks.en: If he gave a get and then made a maamar,
chunks.st: If the yavam gave the yevama a bill of divorce and afterward performed levirate betrothal with her,

chunks.en: she needs a get and chalitzah.
chunks.st: she requires another bill of divorce to cancel the levirate betrothal, as well as ḥalitza to nullify the levirate bond. If

chunks.en: If he gave a get and then married her,
chunks.st: he gave her a bill of divorce and then engaged in intercourse with her,

chunks.en: she needs a get and chalitzah.
chunks.st: she requires a bill of divorce to cancel the betrothal that took place via intercourse, and ḥalitza to nullify the levirate bond; the intercourse did not affect the levirate bond because once he gave her a bill of divorce she was forbidden to him. If

chunks.en: If he gave a get and did chalitzah,
chunks.st: he gave her a bill of divorce and performed ḥalitza,

chunks.en: nothing counts after chalitzah.
chunks.st: nothing is effective after ḥalitza, as the levirate bond was completely nullified.

chunks.en: If he did chalitzah and then made a maamar,
chunks.st: Similarly, if he performed ḥalitza with her and then either performed levirate betrothal,

chunks.en: or gave a get,
chunks.st: or gave a bill of divorce,

chunks.en: or married her; or if he married her and then made a maamar,
chunks.st: or engaged in intercourse with her; alternatively, if he engaged in intercourse with her and then either performed levirate betrothal,

chunks.en: or gave a get or did chalitzah,
chunks.st: or gave a bill of divorce, or performed ḥalitza after they engaged in relations,

chunks.en: nothing counts after chalitzah.
chunks.st: nothing is effective after ḥalitza or intercourse. Any action performed afterward is unrelated to the levirate bond.

chunks.en: It is the same with one yevamah and one yavam
chunks.st: The above principles apply both in cases of one yevama to one yavam,

chunks.en: and with two yevamos and one yavam.
chunks.st: as well as in cases of two yevamot to one yavam.

summary: What happens when a yavam does different acts with two widows of the same brother. The mishnah tells which of them still needs a get or chalitzah.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד. עָשָׂה מַאֲמָר בָּזוֹ וּמַאֲמָר בָּזוֹ,
chunks.en: How so? If he made a maamar with this one and a maamar with that one,
chunks.st: How so? If he performed levirate betrothal with this yevama and levirate betrothal with that one, i.e., her rival wife,

chunks.en: they need two gittin and chalitzah.
chunks.st: they require two bills of divorce, each for her own levirate betrothal, and ḥalitza with one of them, to release them both from the levirate bond. If he performed

chunks.en: A maamar with this one and a get to that one:
chunks.st: levirate betrothal with this one and gave a bill of divorce to that one,

chunks.en: she needs a get and chalitzah.
chunks.st: the first woman requires a bill of divorce to cancel the levirate betrothal, and one of them must receive ḥalitza. If he performed

chunks.en: A maamar with this one and married that one:
chunks.st: levirate betrothal with this one and engaged in intercourse with that one,

chunks.en: they need two gittin and chalitzah.
chunks.st: they require two bills of divorce and he must perform ḥalitza with one of them. If the yavam performed

chunks.en: A maamar with this one and chalitzah with that one:
chunks.st: levirate betrothal with this one and performed ḥalitza with that one,

chunks.en: the first one needs a get.
chunks.st: the first woman requires a bill of divorce. If the yavam gave

chunks.en: A get to this one and a get to that one:
chunks.st: a bill of divorce to this yevama and a bill of divorce to that one,

chunks.en: they need chalitzah from him.
chunks.st: they require ḥalitza from him. If he gave

chunks.en: A get to this one and married that one:
chunks.st: a bill of divorce to this one and engaged in intercourse with that one,

chunks.en: she needs a get and chalitzah.
chunks.st: the latter requires a bill of divorce and ḥalitza. If he gave

chunks.en: A get to this one and a maamar with that one:
chunks.st: a bill of divorce to this one and performed levirate betrothal with that one,

chunks.en: she needs a get and chalitzah.
chunks.st: the latter requires a bill of divorce and he must perform ḥalitza with one of them. If the yavam gave

chunks.en: A get to this one and chalitzah with that one:
chunks.st: a bill of divorce to this woman and performed ḥalitza with that one,

chunks.en: nothing counts after chalitzah.
chunks.st: nothing is effective after ḥalitza, and he cannot betroth the rival wife.

summary: After chalitzah, or after marrying the yevamah, nothing else counts, whether there is one yavam with two yevamos or two yevamin with one yevamah.

chunks.en: If he did chalitzah and chalitzah again,
chunks.st: If he performed ḥalitza with one yevama and then performed ḥalitza with a second yevama,

chunks.en: or chalitzah and then a maamar,
chunks.st: or he performed ḥalitza with one yevama and then proceeded to either perform levirate betrothal,

chunks.en: or gave a get, or married;
chunks.st: give a bill of divorce, or engage in intercourse with a second;

chunks.en: or married and married again,
chunks.st: alternatively, he engaged in intercourse with one yevama and engaged in intercourse with the second yevama,

chunks.en: or married and then made a maamar,
chunks.st: or he engaged in intercourse with one yevama and proceeded to either perform levirate betrothal,

chunks.en: or gave a get, or did chalitzah,
chunks.st: give a bill of divorce, or perform ḥalitza with the second,

chunks.en: nothing counts after chalitzah.
chunks.st: nothing is effective after ḥalitza or intercourse.

chunks.en: This is true with one yavam and two yevamos
chunks.st: These halakhot apply both in cases of one yavam to two yevamot,

chunks.en: and with two yevamin and one yevamah.
chunks.st: as well as two yevamin to one yevama.

summary: Nothing counts after chalitzah, whether it came first, in the middle, or at the end. Marrying is the same only if it came first. Rabbi Nechemyah says both are the same in every order.

chunks.en: If he did chalitzah and then a maamar,
chunks.st: If he performed ḥalitza with one yevama and then proceeded to either perform levirate betrothal,

chunks.en: or gave a get, or married;
chunks.st: give a bill of divorce, or engage in intercourse with a second yevama;

chunks.en: or married and then made a maamar,
chunks.st: alternatively, he engaged in intercourse with one yevama and then proceeded to perform levirate betrothal,

chunks.en: or gave a get, or did chalitzah,
chunks.st: or give a bill of divorce, or perform ḥalitza with a second yevama,

chunks.en: nothing counts after chalitzah,
chunks.st: nothing is effective after ḥalitza,

chunks.en: whether it was at the start,
chunks.st: whether the ḥalitza took place at the beginning,

chunks.en: whether in the middle,
chunks.st: in the middle,

chunks.en: whether at the end.
chunks.st: or at the end.
chunks.stMore: All of these halakhot accord with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, who maintains betrothal does not take effect on a woman who is forbidden due to the prohibition against betrothing a yevama after ḥalitza.

chunks.en: But marrying, if it is at the start,
chunks.st: But with regard to intercourse, when it is at the beginning, i.e., the first act the yavam performed with his yevama,

chunks.en: nothing counts after it.
chunks.st: nothing is effective after it and any subsequent action is void. However, if it was performed

chunks.en: If it is in the middle or at the end,
chunks.st: in the middle, and similarly if it was performed

chunks.en: something can still count after it.
chunks.st: at the end, i.e., after some other action that impairs the validity of his intercourse, something is effective after it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Nechemyah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Neḥemya says:

chunks.en: both marrying and chalitzah,
chunks.st: Both with regard to intercourse and ḥalitza,

chunks.en: whether at the start,
chunks.st: whether performed at the beginning,

chunks.en: whether in the middle,
chunks.st: in the middle,

chunks.en: whether at the end,
chunks.st: or at the end,

chunks.en: nothing counts after it.
chunks.st: nothing is effective after it. If the yavam performed a valid action according to Torah law, any subsequent action is of no consequence according to halakha.
